A1.justification: Despite the changed title and method names, both PDFs describe the same latent-veracity research framework and retain matching experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable in both versions and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original PRONTOQA and GSM8K experiments, search ablations, amortized-inference evaluations, and downstream correction results, including experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and reports additional CommonsenseQA evaluations, Self-Refine integration, block-update comparisons, categorical verification, and correlation analysis.

M1.justification: Search Corrector and Amortized Corrector become VS and AVI; their core reward, greedy initialization, annealing, and pseudo-label training remain unchanged. Appendices C.3–C.5 add bounded procedural extensions: AVI-guided Self-Refine regeneration, contiguous block flips, and categorical-state MCMC.

E1.justification: V2 adds CommonsenseQA, extending evaluation from fictional logical deduction and arithmetic to commonsense multiple-choice reasoning, including naturally generated chains in Self-Refine. Appendix C.5 also introduces verification of True, False, and Unrelated statements. Naturally generated PRONTOQA chains and error-location scenarios already appeared in v1.

E2.justification: New Table 6 evaluates Self-Refine with Many2Many feedback against Self-Refine with AVI; Self-Refine was previously cited but not experimentally compared in this workflow. The existing Recursive, Many2Many, Voting, CoT, random-search, and Best-of-N comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 changes the reported natural-error evaluation from 100 to 1,000 PRONTOQA test problems. New protocols include AVI training on 10,000 examples and one Self-Refine iteration on 1,000 CommonsenseQA questions, categorical verification on 100 examples, and exhaustive evaluation of 128 assignments per seven-statement problem in C.6. Existing core search and fine-tuning settings remain.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses testing whether block updates help, whether verification handles unrelated statements, and whether proxy likelihood aligns with veracity accuracy. It also adds commonsense case studies and the Self-Refine application. These substantially extend methodological diagnosis; the original annealing, initialization, and error-location analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix C.6 introduces Pearson-correlation estimation for each problem and averaging across 100 problems. Existing mean/standard-deviation reporting continues, and C.2 still specifies five runs. Its changed deviations and larger test set do not establish an increased run count.

E6.justification: Retained entries in Tables 1–4 and plotted results in Figures 2–5 are unchanged. V2 adds commonsense, Self-Refine, block-update, categorical, and correlation results in Tables 1 and 6–9. Table 5 replaces raw/baseline/AVI accuracies of 0.71/0.71/0.76 on 100 problems with 0.712/0.697/0.730 on 1,000 problems; this is not a same-setting performance decline. V2 leaves unexplained the Qwen3-4B CommonsenseQA discrepancy between 0.935 in Table 1 and 0.860 for single-bit Metropolis in Table 7.

T1.justification: Appendix C.5 explicitly extends the latent-variable domain from Boolean to k-class categorical vectors, instantiated with True, False, and Unrelated labels; v1 mentioned categorical extensions only as future work. The posterior factorization, reward, Metropolis reasoning, and working hypothesis remain. V2's separate Bayes-rule equation restates existing mathematics rather than adding a proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion redefine the primary contribution around error identification and feedback for correction, whereas v1 foregrounded a self-correction framework. V2 removes the abstract's 'up to 25%' answer-improvement claim, expands claimed coverage to commonsense and categorical verification, and claims demonstrated integration with self-improvement.

C2.justification: V2 replaces the GSM8K explanation about weak numerical perturbations with a distinction between identifying arithmetic errors and recomputing faulty calculations. It adds interpretations concerning harmful correction with unreliable feedback, complementary identification and regeneration, sufficient single-bit updates, and empirical reward alignment. Natural-error benefits are explicitly described as modest, refining applicability beyond the retained synthetic-error limitation.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds CommonsenseQA chain-generation and corruption instructions, prompt templates, and worked prompting examples. New appendices document feedback/refinement model roles, block sizes of 1–3, and examples from the unrelated-statement pool. Existing LoRA, optimizer, hardware, runtime, and search-setting disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially refocused around veracity inference as feedback complementary to self-correction and self-improvement, removing the earlier system-1/system-2 comparison. V2 adds Talmor et al.'s CommonsenseQA and Zhou et al.'s noisy-rationale work while pruning discussions and references including RECONCILE, LM vs LM, and ReST-EM.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. V2 expands the explanation of posterior inference versus direct prompting, reorganizes contribution summaries and related-work subsections, renames the title and methods throughout, and removes the Broader Impact section.

P2.justification: V2 extensively retypesets the document with a compact author block, running headers, different heading styles, and relocated figures and prompt boxes. Table 1 reorders model columns and adds a commonsense block; Tables 6–9 are new displays. Figures 1, 2, and 4 update method labels or legends, while Figures 3 and 5 retain their original images.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens two weaknesses in v1: the central proxy-reward hypothesis lacked a direct test, and downstream utility was demonstrated through negation-based correction. Table 9 supplies direct alignment evidence, while Table 6 tests AVI within a regeneration workflow. The enlarged natural-error evaluation also gives a more restrained account of practical gains, and the revised framing better distinguishes verification from correction. The unexplained CommonsenseQA discrepancy between Tables 1 and 7 weakens reporting, but the gains in empirical support and clarity remain substantial.
